issues.description: The public path-order theorem exports strict ordering for every index pair while admitting the case involving the final path element.
issues.rationale: `lemma_wf_tree_path_nid_increasing` proves only pairs within `drop_last()` and then trusts the remaining final-element case through `admit()`. Callers immediately use the full theorem to exclude the last node from the prefix. Repair 0cc932ae splits the last-index case and derives it from `lemma_is_child_nid_increasing`.

Repair 0cc932ae proves the final-element case from the child relation and removes the assumption.
issues.verification: Source and independent review confirm the unchecked final-element obligation and its checked repair. The historical 323/0 run covers final head only.

issues.description: The write-lock transition exports subtree-lock preservation through an admitted inductive step and an admitted supporting subtree theorem.
issues.rationale: `write_lock_inductive` assumes preservation of `inv_write_lock_cursors_subtree_locked`. The same snapshot also exposes the descendant zero-reader theorem through `admit()`; although it has no direct caller yet, repair 0cc932ae proves and strengthens it, uses its checked wrapper in the write-lock proof, and removes both assumptions. They are one transition-level root.
issues.verification: Source and independent review confirm both assumptions and their common checked repair chain.

issues.description: The write-unlock transition's entire invariant-preservation proof is trusted through `admit()`.
issues.rationale: The transition changes the node to `WriteUnLocked` and downgrades its cursor to `ReadLocking(path.drop_last())`, but its callable inductive proof is wholly admitted. Final repair 7df760c2 proves preservation of the cursor/reader-count relation.
